placements.why: The envelope reports a calibrated instrument verified against a dated reference standard, holding across an operating band — an organizational record-keeping concern (instrument readiness state) that nothing in the existing (currently empty) strata covers. This names a category future calibration envelopes will keep filing under, not a one-time fact.
placements.title: Instrument calibration becomes its own organizational category, tracked as a verifiable operational state rather than a one-off event
placements.frame: Does this content describe an instrument's calibration/verification status against a reference standard, as an ongoing organizational concern rather than a single incident?

placements.title: An instrument's readiness is established by verifying its calibration against a dated reference standard across the full operating range
placements.frame: Was this instrument's calibration checked against a named reference standard, and does it hold across the whole range it's meant to serve?
placements.why: All three segments converge on one theme: the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration state was verified against the June reference plates and holds across the full observing band. This is a subject future envelopes about instrument calibration will keep feeding (new instruments, new reference dates, new bands), not a single fact — so it earns its own leaf under the newly minted Calibration strata rather than being folded as evidence into something else, since no existing leaf structure was supplied to hold it.
